senses.gloss: a ladle or small vessel used for taking liquid out of a larger vessel, esp. for pouring over the hands before and after meals, before prayer &c.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 40:31">Targ. Y. Ex. XL, 31</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 30:21">Ib. XXX, 21</cite> <cite ref="N00559"><he>נְטִילָא</he></cite> f.

senses.gloss: (as a measure) one fourth of a Log.
units: Ḥull. 107ᵃ אתקין … נ׳ בת וכ׳ R. J. ordered that a naṭla (to be used for washing hands) must contain one fourth of a Log; (Rashi: had a standard naṭla made, containing &c.).
Gitt. 69ᵃ bot. נ׳ בת מחוזא a Moḥazean naṭla.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:3:10">Y. Sabb. III, 6ᵃ</cite> bot. [read:] <he>הבא ע״י נ׳ והיא … כלי שני</he> get the hot water into the basin by means of a ladle, when it (the basin) becomes a ‘secondary vessel’ (v. <cite ref="U01589"><he>שֵׁנִי</he></cite>; cmp. Bab.
<cite ref="Berakhot 51a:19">Ber. 51ᵃ</cite> <he>מעטר ליה בנ׳</he> surrounded the large cup (over which the benediction was said) with small cups (for distribution).
